newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices follow lead of futures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices follow lead of futures.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices continued to strengthen early Tuesday but then followed futures lower shortly before nomination deadlines, traders said.
NYMEX's September contract retreated to as low as $2.47 this afternoon, shaving 13.5 cents off the new contract high set late Monday.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, swing prices at the Henry Hub were up an average of three cents to the mid-$2.50s, with prices reaching into the low-$2.60s early in the session.
In the Midwest, swing prices remained fairly firm in the mid-$2.40s. Chicago city-gate gas prices were quoted steady at $2.58-2.61.
In the Permian Basin market, prices climbed another five cents to about $2.48-2.50, with deals reported done anywhere from $2.52 to $2.45. Waha values were equally higher at $2.49-2.52.

El Paso's Keystone Mainline Station, in Winkler County, Texas, will be down through Thursday for maintenance, affecting about 400 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) at the receipt points in the Permian Basin and about 185 mmcfd of supply at Waha.
"Right now we're not seeing much impact on scheduled volumes. About 10-30 percent is being cut," one Texas trader said, referring to the El Paso outage.

San Juan basin gas prices held at $2.37-2.42, traders said, while southern California border prices retreated four cents to the mid-$2.50s. The arrival of cooler weather on parts of the West Coast have caused some buyers to shy away from the market.
In the East, prices at the New York city gate rose a few cents to the mid-$2.70s as storage injections continued at a steady pace, traders said.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 60 to 85 bcf.
